pages.quiz:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — MOCK EXAM #5
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which pencil grip is best? (1 mark)
   A. Hold it lightly between the thumb and first finger
   B. Grip it with a fist
   C. Hold it by the end with your teeth
   D. Press it very hard

2. Which is a good way to practise the shape of a letter? (1 mark)
   A. Trace it in the air with your finger
   B. Ignore it
   C. Rub it out
   D. Cover it

3. The word I is always written (1 mark)
   A. in brackets
   B. with a comma
   C. as a small letter
   D. as a capital letter

4. Which answer is a full sentence for: Why did the pot tip over? (1 mark)
   A. The pot tipped over because Otieno touched the handle.
   B. Handle
   C. Because
   D. Otieno

5. Which of these is a safety rule from the road safety dialogue? (1 mark)
   A. Play on the road
   B. Look right, then left, then right again
   C. Run across without looking
   D. Cross anywhere

6. What is a proverb? (1 mark)
   A. A short wise saying that gives advice
   B. A page of a book
   C. A very long story
   D. A type of number

7. What is extensive reading? (1 mark)
   A. Reading only the title
   B. Copying a book
   C. Reading one word only
   D. Reading many books widely for pleasure

8. What is the difference between a proverb and a story? (1 mark)
   A. A story is shorter
   B. A proverb has many characters
   C. They are the same
   D. A proverb is a short saying and a story is longer with events

9. What is a portfolio of proverbs? (1 mark)
   A. A folder where proverbs are collected and kept
   B. A poem
   C. A game
   D. A kind of bag for money

10. Why might a class record narrations on a device? (1 mark)
   A. To erase them
   B. To listen back and improve
   C. To waste time
   D. To sell them

11. Which value should be shown in a market skit? (1 mark)
   A. Rudeness
   B. Honesty, such as giving correct change
   C. Stealing
   D. Cheating

12. What are the two main parts of a sentence? (1 mark)
   A. Capital and full stop
   B. Noun and verb only
   C. Subject and predicate
   D. Title and ending

13. Which is a wild animal? (1 mark)
   A. Zebra
   B. Dog
   C. Hen
   D. Cow

14. Why are stories important in communities? (1 mark)
   A. They teach values and keep history
   B. They cause trouble
   C. They hide the truth
   D. They waste time

15. What is an interjection? (1 mark)
   A. A word that shows position
   B. A short word that shows a sudden feeling
   C. A word that names a thing
   D. A word that joins sentences

16. What is a talent? (1 mark)
   A. A kind of food
   B. A skill you are good at
   C. A book
   D. A rule

17. What should you do in a reading competition? (1 mark)
   A. Read clearly with the right intonation
   B. Whisper
   C. Read very fast
   D. Shout

18. What is a stage direction? (1 mark)
   A. The title
   B. The ending
   C. An instruction to the actor placed in brackets
   D. A price

19. Which of these can begin a happy line? (1 mark)
   A. Yuck!
   B. Oh no!
   C. Ouch!
   D. Hurray!

20. What is a digital device? (1 mark)
   A. A wooden tool
   B. A machine that works with electronic signals to help us communicate or work
   C. A kind of fruit
   D. A type of song

21. Why do we match devices to their uses? (1 mark)
   A. To break them
   B. To hide them
   C. To know what each is for
   D. To lose them

22. Which word in a small silver radio is the noun? (1 mark)
   A. radio
   B. small
   C. a
   D. silver

23. What should you do before buying a product that an advert says is the best in the world? (1 mark)
   A. Buy it at once
   B. Check it and the price
   C. Send money to a stranger
   D. Believe everything

24. What does N/A mean? (1 mark)
   A. Next assignment
   B. No answer always
   C. Not applicable
   D. New address

25. Which pair of verbs shows an action? (1 mark)
   A. vote, count
   B. red, blue
   C. table, chair
   D. is, are

26. What should you do when someone else is speaking? (1 mark)
   A. Draw
   B. Leave
   C. Talk over them
   D. Listen without interrupting

27. What does turn taking mean? (1 mark)
   A. Speaking all at once
   B. Speaking one at a time and waiting for your chance
   C. Refusing to speak
   D. Speaking loudest

28. Which two words in the poem Lead with honesty rhyme? (1 mark)
   A. leader and rule
   B. fair and strong
   C. all and call
   D. poem and song

29. What is the message of a poem? (1 mark)
   A. The main idea the poet wants to share
   B. The printer
   C. The number of lines
   D. The date

30. What should each step in written instructions usually start with? (1 mark)
   A. A verb
   B. A name
   C. A number only
   D. A colour

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. State two uses of a full stop and a capital letter in a sentence. (2 marks)

32. List the six elements of a story. (3 marks)

33. Explain why leaders are important and why people should obey fair leaders. Give two examples of leaders in a community. (5 marks)

34. Give three signal words used to show the order of steps. (3 marks)

35. Write a short story of five sentences that ends with the proverb A stitch in time saves nine. (5 marks)

36. Give two conjunctions used to join sentences. (2 marks)

37. Plan a short oral narrative about a school rule. Say the characters, the events, the ending, and where you will use a simile and a metaphor. (5 marks)

38. What is a paragraph and what is its main idea? (2 marks)

39. Write one correct line of a dialogue with a speaker name and an interjection. (2 marks)

40. What is a conjunction? Give one example. (2 marks)

41. Give three rules for good turn taking. (3 marks)

42. Explain the difference between a simile and a metaphor and give an example of each. (4 marks)

43. Write four numbered steps for crossing a road safely. (4 marks)

44. Complete with a preposition: The cat sleeps ______ the bed. (2 marks)

45. Name three headings in a story plan. (3 marks)

46. List three habits of an attentive listener. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — MOCK EXAM #5 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — Hold it lightly between the thumb and first finger
   A light grip prevents tiredness.

2. A — Trace it in the air with your finger
   Tracing helps the hand remember the movement.

3. D — as a capital letter
   In English the word I is always a capital.

4. A — The pot tipped over because Otieno touched the handle.
   A full sentence has a subject and a verb and gives the reason.

5. B — Look right, then left, then right again
   The dialogue teaches how to look before crossing.

6. A — A short wise saying that gives advice
   Proverbs teach lessons in a few words.

7. D — Reading many books widely for pleasure
   Extensive reading means reading a lot for enjoyment.

8. D — A proverb is a short saying and a story is longer with events
   Proverbs are very short.

9. A — A folder where proverbs are collected and kept
   A portfolio holds the class collection.

10. B — To listen back and improve
   Recordings show what to improve.

11. B — Honesty, such as giving correct change
   Skits can show good values.

12. C — Subject and predicate
   Every sentence has a subject and a predicate.

13. A — Zebra
   Zebras live freely on the plains.

14. A — They teach values and keep history
   Stories teach and entertain.

15. B — A short word that shows a sudden feeling
   Interjections show emotion.

16. B — A skill you are good at
   A talent is a natural ability.

17. A — Read clearly with the right intonation
   Clear reading with expression is judged.

18. C — An instruction to the actor placed in brackets
   Stage directions tell how to speak or move.

19. D — Hurray!
   Hurray shows happiness.

20. B — A machine that works with electronic signals to help us communicate or work
   Phones and computers are digital devices.

21. C — To know what each is for
   Knowing the use helps us choose the right device.

22. A — radio
   Radio names the thing.

23. B — Check it and the price
   Adverts try to persuade so we check.

24. C — Not applicable
   N/A means the question does not apply.

25. A — vote, count
   Vote and count are actions.

26. D — Listen without interrupting
   Respectful listening is key.

27. B — Speaking one at a time and waiting for your chance
   Turn taking is orderly speaking.

28. C — all and call
   All and call have the same ending sound.

29. A — The main idea the poet wants to share
   The message is the main idea.

30. A — A verb
   Steps begin with action words.

SECTION B
----
31. (2 marks)
   Answer: A capital letter begins a sentence and a full stop ends it.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each correct use.

32. (3 marks)
   Answer: Title, characters, setting, problem, events, ending.
   Working / marking points: Award 3 marks for all six, 2 marks for four or five, and 1 mark for two or three.

33. (5 marks)
   Answer: Leaders guide, make decisions and keep order. Obeying fair leaders keeps peace and safety. Examples: chief, teacher, class monitor, elders.
   Working / marking points: Two marks for why leaders are important, two marks for obeying and one for examples.

34. (3 marks)
   Answer: first, next, then, after that, finally (any three).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

35. (5 marks)
   Answer: Any five clear sentences with a beginning, problem, ending and the proverb used correctly.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each sentence up to four and one mark for using the proverb correctly.

36. (2 marks)
   Answer: and, but, or, so (any two).
   Working / marking points: One mark each.

37. (5 marks)
   Answer: Any plan with characters, events in order, an ending with a lesson, and one simile and one metaphor, for example a pupil who came late but learned that rules are like a map.
   Working / marking points: One mark each for characters, events, ending, simile and metaphor.

38. (2 marks)
   Answer: A paragraph is a group of sentences about one topic. The main idea is what it is mostly about.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each part.

39. (2 marks)
   Answer: Neema: Wow! The sun is shining.
   Working / marking points: One mark for name with colon and one for an interjection.

40. (2 marks)
   Answer: A conjunction is a joining word, such as and, but or when.
   Working / marking points: One mark for the meaning and one for an example.

41. (3 marks)
   Answer: Wait for the speaker to finish, keep your turn short, do not always speak first, listen politely.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each rule.

42. (4 marks)
   Answer: A simile compares using like or as, for example as quick as lightning. A metaphor says one thing is another, for example Time is money.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each definition and one for each example.

43. (4 marks)
   Answer: 1. Stop at the edge. 2. Look right, left and right. 3. Listen for vehicles. 4. Cross when the road is clear.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each correct step in a sensible order.

44. (2 marks)
   Answer: under (or on, if it sleeps on top)
   Working / marking points: One mark for a preposition and one for a sentence that makes sense.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: Title, characters, setting, problem, events, ending (any three).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each heading.

46. (3 marks)
   Answer: Face the speaker, stay quiet, think about the words, wait for your turn, respond correctly (any three).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each habit, up to three.
